newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Scandalised Belgians lose confidence in justice.
newsitem.headline: Scandalised Belgians lose confidence in justice.

text.p: Belgians, reeling from months of child sex scandals and political skulduggery, have lost confidence in their government and legal system, according to an opinion poll published on Friday.
The poll, in Le Vif L'Express weekly magazine, covered 1,000 people broadly split between the country's French and Dutch speaking halves.
On average only three percent of people had full confidence in the centre-left coalition government, whereas 37 percent had no confidence at all, the poll showed.

The Francophone Socialist Party partner in the four-party coalition has been repeatedly hit by allegations it accepted bribes in the late 1980s from French aerospace firm Dassault and Italian helicopter manufacturer Agusta.

The poll also showed that following the scandals of child kidnappings, rapes and murders since August, and the bungled police investigations at the time of the disappearances, people have lost faith in the justice system.
Only three percent of the people polled had complete faith in the justice system against 36 percent who had none.

At the same time only five percent of people had complete faith in the gendarmerie -- which has come in for scorching criticism along with the country's other two police forces -- for gross incompetence or worse in its investigations into the disappearances and murders of five young girls.
On Friday parliament was on the second day of a debate on a special report on the bungled murder investigations.
The crucial question facing parliament, which will vote on the report later on Friday, will be whether party politics can be kept out of the way.

In October more than 250,000 people marched through Brussels in sympathy with the child victims and their parents, but also as a show of disgust at a system seen by most as being incompetent and by many as being corrupt.
